metadata.document_scope: Adds only items not already in Master Plan and Addenda 1-4. Free-only. Milestones follow v5. IDs use prefix W (reference-derived) and V (own ideas) to avoid collisions.

deepseek_harness_behavior_findings: Everything is a plugin: core features are plugins on a composable runtime built on Cordis; a paper is cited in the README (W1.1).
Single-command web launch `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` serves a Web UI at 127.0.0.1:3080 and auto-opens the browser locally (W1.2).
SSH-aware launch prints only the host URL over SSH; the client/editor owns the forwarded address (W1.3).
--no-open flag; Web and Desktop targets from one codebase (apps/, native/, Makefile targets) (W1.4).
Test taxonomy is config-driven: unit, bench, e2e, expected (golden outputs), snapshot, web, web-stress, web-perf, plus pytest.ini (W1.5).
benchmarks/ with BENCHMARK.md and a snapshots/ folder at repo root (W1.6).
Staged-only lint (.oxlintrc.staged.json), lefthook.yml hooks, .jscpd.json duplicate-code detector, .rgignore, .gitattributes, .editorconfig (W1.7).
Dual CI config (.github and .gitlab-ci.yml) in one repo (W1.8).
i18n.yaml single-source docs: README/CONTRIBUTING/SAFETY/BRAND_GUIDELINES i18n YAML alongside .md and .zh.md (W1.9).
SAFETY.md is surfaced as a first-run notice: 'review the safety notice before running' (W1.10).
Developer-preview banner explicitly warns that compatibility-breaking changes will happen (W1.11).
BRAND_GUIDELINES file exists and is localized (W1.12).
Builder instruction files for multiple AI tools: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/, .claude/ (W1.13).
Plugin discoverability through the `dsh-plugin` repository topic (W1.14).
A python/ package exists inside a TS monorepo; contents unknown (W1.15).
patches/ and vendor/ folders for patched/vendored dependencies (W1.16).
Discussions-only feedback (no Issues tab), Discord, citation block, docs site, website folder (W1.17).

Opencode findings used as behaviour evidence: last-match-wins rules, default-ask exceptions, external_directory default allow, shell scanner that refuses on parse failure, MCP OAuth/CIMD/DCR, prompt commands with `!` shell injection outside permission flow, session ID in _meta.
defensive_patterns: Default-ask baseline; no matching permission rule means ask (W3.1).
Deliberately stricter than opencode: Keel defaults `external_directory` to ask (Cautious/Balanced), allow only in Trusted (C-2, W3.6).
Shell scanner for Bash/Zsh/sh/PowerShell: 'cannot analyze' means refuse or force ask, never allow (W3.7).
Prefer narrow allowlists over trying to recognize every dangerous command; presets ship allowlist-style (W3.13).
Saved 'always' approvals are project-scoped, never override a configured deny, and reject cascades to all other pending requests in the session (W3.9).
Policies layer can only hard-deny after rules and saved approvals; policy never grants (W3.10).
MCP server instructions are injected as tainted/untrusted text, lower priority than user instructions (W4.11).
Keel sends no session ID by default (W4.13); opaque per-server correlation IDs instead (V6).
Command `!` shell injection goes through the permission gate and Tier 2, with the resolved command shown before first run (W5.4, C-3).
Secrets staged via file/fd, never argv; narrow-scope keys, never shown on screen/recordings (W7.5, W7.20).
AES-256-GCM sealed secrets/cookies with random IV, AAD, HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure, revocations table (W7.3).
CSRF origin checks, same-origin-only return paths, redirected-link binding to initiating browser, and per-client/global rate limits (W7.7-W7.9).
SSRF protection pins the resolved IP and re-checks every redirect; streaming body-size enforcement (W7.10-W7.11).
Generic client errors with request id; details only in local server log (W7.12).
Security headers and rendering safety: CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, HSTS, nosniff, no raw HTML, scheme allow-list, sandboxed previews (W7.13-W7.14).
Server-side watch-only enforcement; remote-initiated risky actions need local one-time confirmation (Y2.14, W7.19, V9).
Atomic spending caps before each vendor call (W7.18); private vulnerability reporting and support policy (W7.20).
Negative tests first for anything security-relevant; [S] items off by default behind an experimental flag (Section 7).
clean_room_specs: Reimplement from behavior only (X0.10); no [T] row may be built from copied code.

Do not adopt Cordis: Keel is Python. Clean-room equivalent is a plugin scope tree (V1) where providers, tools, channels, UI panels, memory backends and built-in agents register through one plugin API.
Every DS row is README/tree-level only; the package/app/plugin list is unknown and must be verified in M0 before implementation.
Verify SAFETY.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, BENCHMARK.md, BRAND_GUIDELINES.md and the Cordis paper in M0 (currently unread).

Every V row (and any other [S] row) must record: Why (2+ similar products by category), Free check (license/date, reject paid/account-gated/non-commercial), spec in Keel's words, smallest slice behind an experimental flag, negative tests first, end-to-end and offline run ids, owner review before enabling by default (Section 7).

Keel-specific rewrites rather than copies: `keel web` port/flags, private plugin index instead of public dsh-plugin topic, private benchmark folder, in-app redacted feedback bundle, private docs site with no source links.
capability_seams: Single plugin registration API for providers, tools, channels, UI panels, memory backends and built-in agents (W1.1).
Plugin scope tree: child scopes inherit parent permissions only down, never up; unload disposes all registered tools/hooks/routes/panels/timers/subprocesses (V1).
Hidden maintenance agents (compaction, title, summary) map to model roles and are not user-selectable (W2.3).
Per-agent launch allowlist controls which subagents may be started; child permissions are independent, not a subset (W2.6).
MCP prompts imported as slash commands; MCP elicitation and opencode question cards share one UI form (W4.10, W4.12, W8.4).
External specialist adapters let Keel delegate to a coding CLI the user already has, with one-writer-per-tree locking and mandatory diff/test verification (W6.4, V8).
Control-plane routing hints prefer a healthy local desktop tool, then browser tools for DOM work (W6.5).
Local API tokens for CLI/IDE/phone clients; optional per-server opaque correlation id in MCP _meta only when advertised (W7.4, V6).
Community feedback and extension docs stay private; no Keel-operated server required for MCP CIMD (W1.14, W1.17, W4.4).
licensing_notes: DeepSeek Harness is MIT-licensed with THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; verify LICENSE text and every vendor/ license in M0 before reading any code (W1.18).
Vendored code lives in vendor/ with its license file and a PATCHES.md listing each local modification and upstream issue (W1.16).
jscpd duplicate-code detector is MIT - verify license before use (W1.7, V10).
Free-only constraint: reject anything paid, account-gated or non-commercial-only; record each library/model/service with license and verification date (Section 7).
External specialist adapters must never bundle third-party CLIs and must respect each tool's terms (V8).
MCP CIMD must not require a Keel-operated hosted metadata server; fall back to DCR or user-supplied client IDs (W4.4).
conflicts: C-1: rule order - Master 6 'first match wins' vs opencode 'last match wins'; pick one, document everywhere, record in DECISIONS.md; recommendation last-match-wins for Tier 1 with deny-aggregation for multi-resource ops and Tier 2 always above.
C-2: opencode allows everything including external_directory; Keel is intentionally stricter (W3.6). List in PLAN-INDEX.json under 'Deliberate differences'.
C-3: opencode `!`cmd`` runs outside permission flow and sends session id to remote MCP servers; Keel does neither (W5.4, W4.13). Intentional.
C-4: openman watch-only is client-side only; orgo-teammates enforces on server. Keel chooses server-side (Y2.14, W7.19).
C-5: nicks-stack persona asks for no ethics/propriety disclaimers and aggressive behaviour; adopt rigor and anti-sycophancy only (W6.3), never remove safety behavior.
C-6: opencode agents/permissions/mcp-servers/commands docs are now read; remove from M0 list.
C-7: opencode MCP pool/protocol fields refer to a 2026-07-28 MCP revision; treat as [T] for opencode only and verify against official MCP spec in M0.
builder_protocol_for_S_items: Why: one paragraph with the user problem and 2+ similar products or standards by category (no copying).
Free check: each library/model/service, license, date verified; reject paid, account-gated or non-commercial-only.
Spec in Keel's words: behavior, edge cases, failure modes, permissions touched, data stored, Tier-2 interactions.
Smallest slice behind an `experimental` flag; off by default if it touches network, personal data or permissions.
Negative tests first for security-relevant behavior, then positive tests.
End-to-end evidence run id plus an offline run (X0.8).
Owner review before enabling by default if it stores new personal data, makes a network call or changes approval behavior.
priority_order: Resolve C-1 to C-7 first; add to DECISIONS.md.
Permission engine parity and stricter defaults: W3.1-W3.10, W3.13, V2, V5, V12.
Security hardening for keel web/API: W7.3-W7.14, W7.17.
Everything else with its milestone; P2 after the v1.0 candidate is green. Every row goes into PLAN-INDEX.json with its source tag.
